reason: The task proves the global Poitou-Tate sequence for arbitrary two-term torus complexes over a positive-characteristic global field, including the two genuinely necessary completion corrections. Even granting single-coefficient finite-flat duality and the stated local pairings, the retained solution must build compatible compact-support topology, control finite and nonfinite p-primary Kummer systems, remove divisible kernels through Tate modules, stabilize finite D-groups to Sha, and justify both limit exactness and dual exactness for the restricted-product groups. These are interacting global arithmetic and topological obligations; a formal five-lemma step or a previously known Poitou-Tate theorem does not supply them. On the full read scope I independently support H3, with the application-scope and source-display notes below required before configuration approval.
core_assessment: Read every source line196-2617 continuously. Compact-support localization and the two devissages produce the required functorial exact sequences; the local finite-group topology and discrete global images are used to obtain profinite compact-support groups. For tori, splitting by finite etale covers, units/class groups, Kummer and Brauer-Hasse-Noether give the actual finite/cofinite bounds, with U proper where necessary. The class E of profinite-by-finitely-generated groups gives A embedded in A-completed and agreement of finite torsion, so completion is not silently assumed exact for arbitrary groups. The finite-flat torsion pairings are passed through the four Kummer diagrams: the proof distinguishes the finite systems from possibly infinite p-primary profinite systems, and expressly avoids the invalid direct-limit argument in the exceptional degrees1737-1741. Tate modules are torsion-free, their dual kernels divisible, and the finitely generated end cases eliminate those kernels. This supplies the open-curve dualities actually used. D-groups are finite on sufficiently small proper opens and stabilize to the three Sha pairings. The ptstart inverse limits use finite first kernels or surjective kernel transition maps, not an unrestricted claim that inverse limits preserve exactness. The global image discreteness makes the final sequences strict. Local annihilator duality then identifies precisely the two completed low-degree restricted products, while the H^0(character complex) product dual gives an ordinary direct sum. This proves the counted12-term sequence with its two specified exceptions.
prerequisite_assessment: The allowed base inputs are used in their stated roles: one finite-flat coefficient duality, local torus-complex pairings/unramified annihilators, derived localization/Kummer tools, classical cohomological dimension and global-field arithmetic, and dual exactness for strict groups with an open-subgroup basis. I read the supplied local-duality scope note; the stated local Theorems3.1/3.3 are not silently replaced by a number-field-only result. The elementary finite-flat topological base properties explicitly invoked at376-378,423 and444 are part of this base-coefficient apparatus and should remain visible in the prerequisite description. No global Poitou-Tate theorem is permitted as input.

issues.decision: Over U=Spec(F_p[t]), multiplication by t on alpha_p gives a map between finite-flat group schemes whose kernel has coordinate algebra F_p[t,x]/(x^p,t*x), not flat over F_p[t]. Thus taking A=ker(f_r) in the general finite-flat devissage does not automatically keep the induction inside finite-flat groups. In this task the complexes actually used in1349 are built from n-torsion of tori (finite multiplicative type) and their Cartier-dual finite etale groups. These subcategories are etale-locally finite modules under Cartier duality, so their kernels and quotients remain finite flat, and the author induction applies to the needed cases. State this application boundary visibly; do not invent a proof for arbitrary finite-flat complexes.
issues.resolution: I read the r002 visible application note. It certifies only the multiplicative-type torus-torsion/dual finite-etale subclasses used by the counted theorem, so it does not claim to repair or prove the unnecessary arbitrary finite-flat kernel assertion.

issues.mathematical_target_assessment: Resolved for the final theorem because2539-2540 works throughout on U!=X and such opens are cofinal.
issues.decision: The finiteness arguments and finite D-pairings invoke results with U!=X. This assumption must be carried visibly into the preliminary finite D statements. At U=X, for example C=G_m gives D^1(X,C)=Pic(X), which need not be finite; so the unqualified finite-group wording cannot be certified literally. The final Poitou-Tate proof already takes a proper open, so no change to its counted hypotheses is needed.
issues.resolution: The r002 note explicitly carries U!=X into the finite D-pairing application and preserves the final theorem scope. The U=X literal finiteness claim is not endorsed.

corrections.detail: 431 uses H^1 where its diagram428 has H^i. In435 the quotient defining H_c^i uses degree i-1 as in405, not degree i.

The character-complex row must follow devis2 (553-555), with T2 then T1, rather than the swapped row in882-886; the initial0 is not a general injectivity assertion. Use the relevant segment of the already printed long exact sequence.
C_(r+11) is C_(r+1), fixed by the displayed complex and1306.
The middle lower Kummer group is H^(i+1)(U,C tensor^L Z/ell^m), not H^(i+2); both adjacent groups and avfini1 determine the index.
The second upper H_c^2(character torus) is T1, not a repeatedT2, as fixed by devis2 and the lower row.
The group whose D^2 injects into D^2(hat M) is D^2(U,hat C), not D^2(U,hat T), by the stated goal2031 and triangle545.

The shrinking-open argument uses the covariant maps on compact-support groups and their D images, together with the injective restriction into H^r(K,hat C); it does not assert a reverse map on ordinary H^r(V)->H^r(U). The needed commutative diagram is278-299.
The leading0 before H^0(F)->H^1(T) is not needed or generally correct; the relevant long exact segment suffices because the H^0(F) restriction is an isomorphism.
H^1(K,hat C) in a proof for general i is H^i(K,hat C), as the following D^i argument specifies.
The duality for H_c^(i+1)(C) is refin1(a), source1857-1866, rather than the cited refin2; invariance of low character cohomology is finityp(a), source837-840.
